respuesta.pregunta: Which version of 2p-revenue-optimizer-api documents which base images to put in the Dockerfile and Dockerfile.runtime for the release process?
respuesta.respuesta:
Both versions in the documentation I retrieved, 0.2.2 and latest, document this, and their Release Process sections say the same thing.

In 0.2.2, the first usage step is to set the correct tag in your `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.runtime` for the Java runtime version you want. The examples are `FROM hub.vendorflow-cloud.io/vendorflow/java:17-mini` for the `Dockerfile` and `FROM hub.vendorflow-cloud.io/vendorflow/java:17-runtime-mini` for the `Dockerfile.runtime` [2p-revenue-optimizer-api/0.2.2/guide/README.md:L67-L79]. Links to the lists of available tags for each file are also there [2p-revenue-optimizer-api/0.2.2/guide/README.md:L74-L81].

The latest README has the same step and the same two base images: `java:17-mini` for the `Dockerfile` and `java:17-runtime-mini` for the `Dockerfile.runtime` [2p-revenue-optimizer-api/latest/guide/README.md:L67-L79]. It also links to the same tag lists [2p-revenue-optimizer-api/latest/guide/README.md:L74-L81].

For questions about the release process, both versions point to the Release Process Issue Tracker [2p-revenue-optimizer-api/0.2.2/guide/README.md:L85-L87] [2p-revenue-optimizer-api/latest/guide/README.md:L85-L87].
answer_checks: Identifies both 0.2.2 and latest as versions that document the Dockerfile/Dockerfile.runtime base image tags.
States that the content is the same in both versions (java:17-mini for Dockerfile and java:17-runtime-mini for Dockerfile.runtime).
Cites the README.md Release Process section of both 0.2.2 and latest.
Does not claim that these are the only versions of the software or that other versions lack this information.
Does not ask the user for a version and does not add base image tags or details not present in the documents.
